fields.v: Not a spec-to-code flow. Agent protocol: start session by reading instructions, summary and project map (Setup Mode populates them on a new project, Maintenance Mode afterwards) -> call precheck_file before modifying a file -> log issue before attempting a fix -> record each attempt with outcome -> record fix when there is evidence -> record decisions/notes; git pre-commit hook runs the gate as fallback. Nothing is enforced

fields.v:
No agent/model configurations with task outcomes; models never stated.
- projectmem v0.3.3 gate (latency, synthetic repo): 56.7 / 61.8 / 79.3 ms median at 100 / 400 / 1,500 events; 2 git calls. Criteria stated by the authors: gate cost 'should not grow with the age of a project'; same warnings as before. Quality: works (same failed-attempt warning in every configuration); cost: works (nearly constant, under 83 ms)
- projectmem v0.3.2 gate (baseline, latency): 2,748 / 11,286 / 42,047 ms; 100 / 400 / 1,500 git calls. Quality: works (same warnings); cost: does not work (grows in proportion to the log)
- v0.3.3 + Antigravity 2.1.4 + model n.s.: acceptance suite T1-T4 (authors' pass criteria) all pass. Quality: works; cost: works (T4 checks gate cost; no values per client)
- v0.3.3 + Claude desktop app Code tab 2.9939.2 + model n.s.: T1 resolution only, T2 pass, T3 read path only, T4 pass after fix (two defects found and fixed). Quality: partly; cost: works after fix (T4)
- v0.3.3 + Codex 26.908.40834 + model n.s.: T1-T4 pass. Quality: works; cost: works (T4)
- Cursor 3.4.17: not run
- Scripted reversal task, 1 run in each of two MCP clients (not named), model n.s.: agent recorded the supersession unprompted in both. Quality: works (authors: a demonstration, not a measurement); cost: not measured
- Self-study (authors' use, agents and models n.s.): 3,228 events; 86 of 427 fixed issues (20%) had a failed attempt before the fix; prevention not measured. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- Cross-project store (macOS): 12 of 46 lessons (26%) correctly attributed, 5 (11%) ambiguous, 29 (63%) wrong; authors call it 'a defect in the implementation' but state no success criterion. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: N/A

fields.v: No measure of prevention (benchmark proposed); file-scoped advisory gate cannot tell whether a change repeats a failure; depends on capture completeness; no semantic recall; summary grows with history (~30,000 tokens in one project); non-atomic writes, fail-open redaction; schema and instructions changed during the study; self-study of own projects dominated by one project; token figures estimates; single-user. Future: repeat-failure benchmark, gate instrumentation, supersession traversal, better attribution, tool-call boundary gate, open event schema, shared team memory
